Theme

Household, washing & chores · Time, the calendar & feasts

alarm clock noun

also alarm, the alarm went off

modern

Traupman 122: suscitābulum sonuit, the alarm went off

suscitābulum, suscitābulī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

alarm

In Varro only “a rousing”, so the alarm is a modern sense.

Other words

  • hōrologium suscitātōrium

    also used · modern · Traupman 122

  • hōrologium excitātōrium — alarm clock

    also used · Renaissance · Vives, Exercitatio (M-O s.v. alarm clock)

    Vives’s phrase; excitātōrius is not in Lewis & Short.

  • excitātōrium, excitātōriī n. — alarm clock

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Andresian p. 3 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Vives’s adjective made a noun; not in Lewis & Short.

Examples

  • Nōndum lūcēbat, cum suscitābulum sonuit.

    It was not yet light when the alarm went off.Libellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

  • Suscitābulum sonuit.

    The alarm went off.Traupman 270

See also wall clock.
